card.label: S. 3977
card.summary: The Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment Act of 2026 restores certain debt limit increases for small business reorganizations (Subchapter V) and wage earner bankruptcies (Chapter 13) that had expired in 2024. The bill raises the debt limit for small businesses from approximately $3.4 million to $7.5 million, and increases the cumulative debt limit for Chapter 13 bankruptcies from approximately $2.1 million to $2.75 million, combining secured and unsecured debt into a single limit for Chapter 13.
card.title: Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment Act of 2026

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment Act of 2026 restores debt limit changes that expired in 2024 for small business reorganizations (Subchapter V) and wage earner bankruptcy plans (Chapter 13). It raises the debt limit for small business bankruptcies to $7.5 million and for Chapter 13 bankruptcies to $2.75 million, while combining secured and unsecured debt limits for Chapter 13.

affected_groups.effect: Can use Subchapter V bankruptcy reorganization with higher debt totals up to $7.5 million.
Can file under Chapter 13 bankruptcy with debt totals up to $2.75 million, combining secured and unsecured debts.

key_provisions: Restores expired debt limits for small business reorganizations and Chapter 13 bankruptcies.
Increases the small business (Subchapter V) debt limit to $7.5 million.
Increases the Chapter 13 bankruptcy debt limit to $2.75 million.
Applies both secured and unsecured debt together toward the Chapter 13 limit.
Applies the new debt limits to any bankruptcy case commenced on or after the date of enactment.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment Act of 2026 restores debt limit changes that expired in 2024 for small business reorganizations (Subchapter V) and wage earner bankruptcy plans (Chapter 13). It raises the debt limit for small business bankruptcies to $7.5 million and for Chapter 13 bankruptcies to $2.75 million, while combining secured and unsecured debt limits for Chapter 13.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters financial eligibility thresholds for specific types of federal bankruptcy filings, making higher-debt small businesses and individual earners eligible for specific reorganization and repayment plans.
